key_insight: Tensor-network decompositions turn a high-dimensional quantum dynamics problem into multiple lower-dimensional, asynchronously runnable tasks across quantum and classical hardware.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical path to distributed quantum simulation with lower gate cost, making it attractive for heterogeneous near-term quantum computing platforms.
method: Represent the multidimensional time-evolution operator as a tensor network.
Map the entangled evolution into independent lower-dimensional propagations in an elevated Hilbert space.
Compile the distributed subproblems on trapped-ion hardware using native partial-entangling XX(θ) gates.
evidence_signal: On a trapped-ion quantum computer, the approach reproduced vibrational spectra of a protonated water cluster within 4 cm^-1 of classical results and reduced expected two-qubit gate infidelity by more than 30% versus standard decompositions.
watch_item: The workflow depends on careful tensor-network decomposition and hardware-aware compilation, so performance and scalability may vary across heterogeneous quantum systems.
paper_title: Tensor-Network-Based Distributed Quantum Dynamics on Independent Quantum Computers
